_comment: Tempdoc 727: sessions excluded from developer-agent friction analysis because they are not organic coding/engineering work on this repo. Classified by hand against each session's judge-produced summary + first user message; scope confirmed with the user 2026-07-14 (business/research sessions excluded, coding/engineering only). Update this file when re-running mine-friction.mjs on new sessions.
_basis: CAPTURED, not derived (tempdoc 858 §9.1). This is a hand classification made once, on 2026-07-14, against the 89 transcripts then present in ~/.claude/projects. Claude Code rotates transcripts away, so the ids below decay: as of 2026-08-19, 0 of the 31 still resolve to a transcript on disk. Reproduce with: count every *.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects RECURSIVELY (5879 files on 2026-08-19 — the recursive walk is the strict check because it also covers nested subagent sidechains; a top-level-only walk sees 4753) and test whether any transcript basename startsWith any key below. It is kept, not deleted, because the classification itself is not recomputable — the evidence it was made from is gone — and because the WHY (three exclusion classes, below) is the durable part a future re-run needs.
_reasoning: The three classes, so the next re-run can reproduce the judgement rather than the ids: (1) benchmark-subject — sessions that are an automated eval-harness burst rather than a person working (14 here, the battlefield-en-v1 burst in a 12-minute window on 2026-07-08); (2) not-this-repo's-engineering — personal/unrelated sessions and business/research sessions (grants, competitor research, GEO, policy) that never touched code; (3) empty — slash-commands only, no task content, which slipped past mine-friction.mjs's <200-char 'too small' threshold because stacked command entries padded them over it. Class (3) is the one a mechanical rule could replace; (1) and (2) need a content judgement, which today only the LLM judge in mine-friction.mjs can make.
_consumers: aggregate-friction.mjs, friction-timeline.mjs, overhead-taxonomy.mjs, baseline-economics.mjs. A consumer MUST NOT report a zero match here as an observed 'nothing needed excluding' — with every id rotated out, a zero means the filter was inert. This is not left to each consumer to honour: all four read the list through loadExclusionKeys/makeExclusionMatcher and render through fmtScopeExclusion in lib/telemetry-io.mjs, which has no output that states a bare zero, and lib/telemetry-io.scope-filter.test.mjs asserts that no input can produce one. Before 858 §7 there were three forked copies of the matcher running two different match rules; add a consumer by importing the shared helpers, not by copying them.
